speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern, but we must quickly rule out kidney stones or infection given your flank pain. Have you noticed any blood clots in your urine, or does the pain radiate to your groin? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CT_Kidney

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance: Reddish, WBC: 10-20 /HPF, RBC: Too numerous to count, Nitrites: Negative, Leukocyte_Esterase: Positive; CT_Kidney: No stones or masses identified. Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medullary Sponge Kidney.

The urinalysis confirms significant hematuria with sterile pyuria, and the CT scan specifically identifies multiple cysts in the medullary collecting ducts, which is the hallmark of Medullary Sponge Kidney. While kidney stones are a common complication, the absence of obstruction or visible stones on your CT points directly to this congenital structural anomaly as the cause of your symptoms.
